alias: Cameras - stale motion alert (daytime pipeline check)
description: Fleet-wide motion-pipeline dead-man, hourly rolling window: pages if NO camera has reported a motion EVENT for 4+ hours, checked hourly during active hours (10:00-20:00). Replaced the twice-daily since-08:00 check after a real Ring event-listener wedge ran ~12h before paging (2026-07-24). REBASED 2026-08-17 onto sensor.camera_motion_stale's recorder-derived hours_since map: the old template read entity last_changed, which (a) resets on every restart, blinding the check for up to 4h, and (b) treated a sensor stuck 'on' as fresh motion - one camera's motion binary_sensor sat latched 'on' for 85h and pinned the staleness clock to zero for ~35 consecutive hourly checks. The recorder survives both. If the staleness sensor itself dies this condition reads false - that hole is covered by the camera_motion_monitor_down dead-man.

conditions.value_template: {% set hs = state_attr('sensor.camera_motion_stale','hours_since') %}{% set vals = (hs or {}).values() | reject('none') | list %}{{ vals | length > 0 and (vals | min) > 4.0 }}

data.title: ⚠️ Cameras: no motion detected today
data.message: {% set hs = state_attr('sensor.camera_motion_stale','hours_since') or {} %}{% set vals = hs.values() | reject('none') | list %}No motion event from ANY camera in the last {{ (vals | min) | round(1) if vals else '?' }} hours (recorder-derived - immune to restarts and stuck sensors). The Ring->Scrypted->MQTT->HA motion pipeline may be down (usual fix: reload the Ring plugin in Scrypted). If HA history is empty for OTHER entity types too, the recorder - not the camera pipeline - is the fault. Checked {{ now().strftime('%-I:%M %p') }}.
